title: 1994 AHSME Problem 13
statement: In triangle \(ABC,\) \(AB=AC.\) If there is a point \(P\) strictly between \(A\) and \(B\) such that \(AP=PC=CB,\) then \(\angle A=\)

solutions.text: Let \(\angle A=\theta.\) Since \(AP=PC,\) triangle \(APC\) has \(\angle PAC=\angle PCA=\theta.\) Since \(AB=AC,\) each base angle of \(\triangle ABC\) is \(\frac{180^\circ-\theta}{2}.\) Also \(PC=CB,\) so the base angles of \(\triangle PCB\) at \(P\) and \(B\) are equal; the one at \(B\) is \(\frac{180^\circ-\theta}{2}.\) Hence \(\angle PCB=\theta.\) At \(C,\) \[ 2\theta=\frac{180^\circ-\theta}{2}, \] giving \(5\theta=180^\circ\) and \(\theta=36^\circ.\) Thus the correct answer is B.
